0.Name: Clean
0.Description: No restriction; a properly groomed appearance is possible.

1.Name: Worn
1.Description: Visible traces of travel or work; normally no mechanical consequence.

2.Name: Dirty
2.Description: Noticeable stains and body odor; social consequences in clean environments.

3.Name: Stinking
3.Description: Strong mud, sweat, blood, or decay odor; obvious in most environments.

Water.Name: Water without soap
Water.Description: 30 minutes, free: reduce dirt by exactly one level.

Soap.Name: Self-wash with soap
Soap.Description: 1 hour, 1 Mark: set body and clothing to level 0.

WashHouse.Name: Wash house or simple inn
WashHouse.Description: Several hours, 2 Mark: set body and clothing to level 0.

Bathhouse.Name: Good bathhouse with launderer
Bathhouse.Description: 1–2 hours, 5 Mark: level 0 and a temporary groomed appearance.

SpareClothing.Name: Clean spare clothing
SpareClothing.Description: 1 minute: clothing becomes clean; body odor remains.

DailyUpkeep.Name: Daily upkeep
DailyUpkeep.Description: 2 Mark per day in a suitable settlement: washing, laundering, drying, and minor repairs.

Clean.Name: Clean
Clean.Description: Noble houses, authorities, temples, wealthy merchants, and formal events.
Clean.Reaction: Heavy dirt suggests poverty, disease, disrespect, or danger.

Ordinary.Name: Ordinary
Ordinary.Description: Villages, harbors, barracks, workshops, and ordinary taverns.
Ordinary.Reaction: Light to moderate dirt is normal; stench draws notice.

PoorLawless.Name: Poor or lawless
PoorLawless.Description: Slums, bandit camps, smuggler dens, and labor districts.
PoorLawless.Reaction: Overly clean clothing can reveal wealth, office, foreignness, or vulnerability.

Wilderness.Name: Wilderness
Wilderness.Description: Travel, camps, and natural environments with scent-based tracking.
Wilderness.Reaction: Stains matter little, but odor can reveal a trail.

Military.Name: Military
Military.Description: Barracks, field camps, garrisons, and military service.
Military.Reaction: Work and travel marks are tolerated; strong odor disrupts discipline and proximity.

Religious.Name: Religious
Religious.Description: Temples, shrines, monasteries, and ritually clean places.
Religious.Reaction: Dirt may be seen as disrespect or ritual impurity.

Court.Name: Court or nobility
Court.Description: Court society, audiences, banquets, and highly formal encounters.
Court.Reaction: Even worn clothing may be considered unsuitable.

Sewer.Name: Sewer
Sewer.Description: Wastewater, feces, rats, chemicals, and stagnant moisture.
Sewer.Reaction: Extreme contamination and sewage stench are likely.

Swamp.Name: Swamp
Swamp.Description: Mud, stagnant water, plant rot, and insects.
Swamp.Reaction: Heavy dirt and difficult-to-hide odor accumulate quickly.

Battlefield.Name: Battlefield
Battlefield.Description: Blood, mud, smoke, sweat, and decay.
Battlefield.Reaction: Blood and decay may count one level worse for social and scent interactions.

Rules.Text1: People judge you by more than your words. Mud on your boots, dried blood on your coat, and clothing worn for days change how you are received, treated, and assessed.
Rules.Text2: You can clean clothing yourself at suitable water, use soap, change into spare clothing, or pay wash houses, bathhouses, and launderers in settlements. A bed alone cleans neither you nor your clothing.
Rules.Text3: Farmers, soldiers, sailors, and laborers do not expect spotless clothing. Merchants, officials, temple servants, and nobles may view heavy dirt as a sign of poverty, disease, disrespect, or danger. In slums and bandit camps, clothing that is too clean may stand out instead. Animals and some monsters do not care about stains—but they do care about sweat, blood, and decay.

RollAdvice.FilthyOrdinary: Stinking in an ordinary environment: complaints, distancing, or worse treatment are possible.
RollAdvice.TooClean: Too clean in a poor or lawless environment: standing out or disadvantage when blending in is possible.
RollAdvice.BlendIn: Appropriately dirty in a labor district: advantage for blending in or disguise is possible.
RollAdvice.IntimidatingFilth: Heavy grime may be intimidating; advantage is situationally possible.

OneShotSelectionButtons.Name: One-press selection buttons
OneShotSelectionButtons.Hint: When enabled, Select visible and Select folder fill the selection once per click and a second click does nothing; clear it with Clear selection. When off (default), these buttons are toggles: they stay highlighted while every selectable row they cover is selected, and clicking a highlighted button empties it again.

SettingsHub.Title: Runyth Garb & Grime — Configuration
SettingsHub.Subtitle: All world rules are grouped by topic. Safe defaults work without initial setup.

General.Title: General presentation
General.Hint: The central manager remains available through Module Settings.
General.ShowSheetIndicator: Show cleanliness indicator on supported actor sheets
General.ShowIndicatorToPlayers: Show indicator to players on owned actors
General.LocalizationHint: Runyth Garb & Grime follows Foundry’s Language Preference and does not maintain a separate language override. Change the language under Game Settings → Configure Settings → Core Settings. A reload may be required.
General.DashboardHint: Open the scalable Actor and party management dashboard directly from the module’s global settings.
General.ActorScopeHint: Limit the dashboard Actor pool before Garb & Grime reads cleanliness summaries or prepares rows. Folder selection and the regular expression are combined; leave both empty to include every supported visible Actor. Character Actors linked to non-GM users through Foundry character assignment or OWNER permission are always included so newly added PCs cannot be hidden by a stale manual scope.
General.ActorScopeRegexHint: Optional. Matches Actor name, Actor type, and full Actor-folder path. Uses Unicode, case-insensitive regular-expression matching.
General.ActorScopeIncludeSubfolders: Include descendants of selected Actor folders
General.ActorScopeFolderHint: No selected folders means all Actor folders. Use the search field to narrow large folder trees before selecting visible folders.
General.ActorScopeNoFolders: No Actor folders exist in this world.

Automation.Title: Automatic dirt gain
Automation.LongRestHint: Disabled by default. Rest alone does not clean.
Automation.CombatEndHint: Enable only if every completed combat causes dirt in your campaign.
Automation.WorldDayHint: Uses Foundry world time and processes characters once per new day.
Automation.OncePerDay: Limit ordinary automatic gain to once per in-game day
Automation.ExtremeBypass: Explicit extreme events may bypass the daily limit

Cleaning.Title: Cleaning methods
Cleaning.Hint: Edit names, costs, currency, time, result, body/clothing, items, effects, and availability.
Cleaning.ItemsHint: Comma-separated stable IDs; present required items are consumed when the method succeeds.
Cleaning.SoapEnforcementHint: Optional GM enforcement for Self-wash with soap. Checks the character inventory for an item tagged as the Soap integration or named Soap/Seife. Other cleaning methods are unaffected. GM bulk clean and system actions can still bypass item requirements. A missing item blocks the wash before currency or cleanliness changes.
Cleaning.RequireSoap: Require soap in the Actor inventory to self-wash with soap
Cleaning.ConsumeSoap: Consume soap from inventory after a successful requirement check
Cleaning.InvalidSoapQuantity: Soap quantity must be a whole number between 1 and 100.

Upkeep.Title: Daily cleanliness upkeep
Upkeep.Hint: Campaign default: 2 Mark per day. Individual actors must also opt in.
Upkeep.DeductionWarning: Automatic deduction remains inactive until payment mode, deduction, and a working adapter are all enabled.

Rolls.Title: Contextual roll advice
Rolls.Hint: Recommendations apply only to configured skills and the current scene context.
Rolls.AdvisoryDefault: Safe default: advisory only. No roll is changed invisibly; automatic mode always displays the reason first.
Rolls.ModePrompt: Pause GM rolls and ask for a mode
Rolls.ModeHint: Players always receive advisory handling. GM prompt mode cancels the pending GM roll, shows four explicit choices, then safely repeats it.

Contexts.Title: Environment profiles
Contexts.Hint: Profiles are activated through scene flags and may be registered by extension modules.
Contexts.SettlementTypesHint: Comma-separated, such as village, town, city, military, or court. A method is available when at least one tag matches.
Contexts.ServicesHint: Comma-separated method IDs that are explicitly available in this profile regardless of tags.
Contexts.RuleJsonHint: Use level0 through level3 keys and values such as normal, disadvantage-social, possible-advantage-blend, or scent-stealth-impossible.
Contexts.LevelRatingsHint: Each preset has an explicit four-level acceptance gradient. These four values are what the Scene guide uses; the legacy expected min/max fields only remain as a fallback for older/custom definitions without classifications.
Contexts.SceneGuideAutoOpen: Open the guide when the viewed Scene changes
Contexts.SceneGuideHint: Keep the current Scene’s expected, accepted, tolerated, disliked, and hated cleanliness levels visible in a small GM-only window.

Contaminations.Title: Contaminations
Contaminations.Hint: Contaminations can worsen the effective level for relevant interactions.

Sheets.Title: Actor sheets, Token HUD, and effects
Sheets.TokenQuickActions: Show quick actions in Token HUD
Sheets.SceneControlsHint: Show Garb & Grime buttons in Foundry’s Scene Controls toolbar for opening the manager, scene context and cleanliness guide. Disabling this removes those toolbar buttons, not any cleanliness rules or stored states.
Sheets.ActiveEffectsHint: Synchronize Actor cleanliness states to module-owned Active Effects. Enabling this creates or updates the related effects; disabling it removes only effects owned by Garb & Grime. This does not change the saved cleanliness states.
Sheets.ContaminationEffectsHint: When Active Effect mirroring is enabled, also synchronize contamination-related effects. This toggle has no effect while Active Effect mirroring is off; contamination data remains intact either way.
Sheets.TokenLabelsHint: Show a compact, high-contrast cleanliness label next to Tokens without replacing Foundry nameplates. Labels are rendered in a dedicated interface layer above all Tokens. The global toggle is stored per client; individual Token display and position overrides are stored in Token flags.
Sheets.TokenLabelsKeybindingHint: The default shortcut is Shift+Alt+G. Change it under Game Settings → Configure Controls → Garb & Grime.
Sheets.TokenLabelsVisibilityModeHint: Choose when inherited cleanliness labels are visible. Per-Token Always show/Always hide overrides still take precedence.
Sheets.TokenLabelsPlayerScopeHint: GM visibility is always allowed. Players must also have the “View persistent cleanliness status” permission.
Sheets.TokenLabelsPlayerViewersHint: Set an explicit exception for individual players. The default role permission is Nobody, so players do not see persistent cleanliness status unless you allow it here or change the role permission.
Sheets.TokenLabelsNoPlayers: No non-GM users exist in this world.
Sheets.TokenLabelsAutomaticModeHint: This display behaviour is controlled by the GM setting. The manual Shift+Alt+G toggle applies only to Manual toggle mode.
Sheets.TokenLabelsPermissionAuthority: Player authorization is controlled only in the Permissions tab. This section controls which permitted Token types are eligible and the GM default presentation.
Sheets.TokenLabelsShortcutEnabledHint: Enable the client-side shortcut action. Change the actual key combination under Game Settings → Configure Controls → Garb & Grime. This does not grant players permission to view labels.
Sheets.TokenLabelsShortcutScopeHint: Default: every player-linked character Token on the current Scene, even when no Token is selected. Selected modes require selecting Tokens first. No world Token flags are changed.
Sheets.TokenLabelsShortcutKeybindingHelp: Shortcut: Shift+Alt+G by default. Every press makes the chosen Token labels all visible or all hidden on your client. Change the keybinding in Foundry’s Configure Controls; Permissions remains authoritative. This works in automatic and manual display modes.

Permissions.Title: Role-based permissions
Permissions.Hint: Ownership rules also apply. Players can never modify unowned actors through this UI.
Permissions.OwnershipHint: Ownership rules still apply. “Nobody” disables a permission for every non-GM user.
Permissions.UserOverridesHint: An exception overrides the minimum role for this user only. Actor ownership still applies to actor-specific actions.

Currency.Title: Currency and adapters
Currency.Hint: Mark remains a distinct campaign currency. A D&D 5e denomination must be mapped deliberately.
Currency.Dnd5eHint: Leave blank to prevent any silent conversion.
Currency.MarkWarning: Default methods use exactly “Mark”. The module never silently converts Mark to GP.

RollChoice.Title: Cleanliness roll decision

RollChoice.AdvantageOpponent: The opposing tracker may have advantage
